components: However, their practical adoption in robot software stacks still depends on reproducible middleware integrations rather than on model quality alone.

Florence-2 is especially attractive in this regard because it unifies captioning, optical character recognition, open-vocabulary detection, grounding and related vision-language tasks within a comparatively manageable model size.

This article presents a ROS 2 wrapper for Florence-2 that exposes the model through three complementary interaction modes: continuous topic-driven processing, synchronous service calls and asynchronous actions.

deploymentClaims: The wrapper is designed for local execution and supports both native installation and Docker container deployment.
A functional validation is reported together with a throughput study on several GPUs, showing that local deployment is feasible with consumer grade hardware.
